* [AI:claude] fix(train): per-train pre-lease ownership so a lease release never closes a sibling train (Refs BUG-2537)

PR #3904 P1: every train opened in one process recorded under
merge-lease:<pid>, so releasing train A's lease closed still-open train B
and moved its riders to Leased. Pre-lease ownership now uses

train takes the lease. Regression opens two trains, takes and releases A's
lease, and proves B and its rider stay Training and refused.

Recovery built its forge port with named:false, so a train resumed by a

carries prs_named_on_command_line; an --all-ready sweep still never
consents, and naming a different PR still never resumes the old train.

* [AI:claude] perf(mandate): gate reads an incremental store-history index (BUG-2554)

The train gate's two full store-history walks (the name-only version
walk and the -G alias walk) ran on every gate and cost about 20 minutes
per train under disk pressure. They now read a persisted, append-only
index in the git common dir (never tracked or pushed). Each read walks
only commits reachable from ref tips not yet indexed. A missing,
corrupt or version-skewed index, or a vanished indexed tip, rebuilds
with one full walk under AIDA_STORE_HISTORY_TIMEOUT_SECS, so a doubt
never reads as "no history". Regressions compare index answers with
the full walk on a long-history fixture, including the BUG-2179
deleted-by-agreed_id case, and assert the refresh walk is bounded.

* [AI:claude] fix(mandate): a narrowing renewal ends live ship covers; a revival keeps its receipt (STORY-2771)

Review round 1 on PR #3961.

- A ship cover records whether the mandate lifted the supervised classes
  when it was issued. The pre-merge and train rechecks read the mandate's
  current flags, so `renew --exclude-supervised` ends covers issued under
  the wider mandate, as `--exclude-gate-paths` already did. The cover does
  not record which spec relied on the lift, so every cover issued under it
  ends; the ship is refused and can be re-run.
- A revival stores its receipt (old id, old expiry, change lines) on the
  fresh record as `revived`, validated against the record's issuance, and
  the audit event for a renewal or revival carries the change lines.
  `aida mandate status` shows the revival.
- The revival message no longer says the flags were retained when the
  renewal changed them.

* [AI:claude] fix(mandate): history index matches --all start points, bounds and anchors (BUG-2554)

Start points now come from `git rev-list --all --no-walk` (every ref and
every worktree HEAD, detached included); a failed probe is an error, not
an unborn HEAD. The anchor check runs under the store-history deadline
(argv, no stdin). Anchors are kept for every retained history (deleted refs
included, minimized with merge-base --independent), so a later gc rebuilds
the index; index version 2 rebuilds older indexes. Non-hex anchors read as
a corrupt index.

* [AI:claude] fix(land): land run counts only a reviewer's own verdict, heads its logs, caps on live reviewers, and survives record IO errors (STORY-2768)

Review round 1 of #3981:
- A reviewer past its limit is excused only by a verdict recorded since it
  started. An older verdict at the same head no longer reads as its work, so
  the head counts its timeouts and derives BLOCKED instead of relaunching
  without end.
- Each child's log starts with what it was launched against: time, changes,
  head, base, merge tree (reviewer), spec (lane) and the command.
- The review cap counts live reviewers this run started as well as rows
  derived as in review, once per change.
- A record of children that cannot be read or written is reported and the
  run goes on; nothing is launched until the record is on disk, and the
  --once wait no longer exits and abandons its children.

* [AI:claude] fix(gate): each change keeps its own verdict when two changes ship one spec (BUG-2570)

A spec key is shared by every change that ships the spec. Its file holds
one verdict, the last written, and its newest ledger event can belong to
another change. With #3972 and #3973 both under STORY-2768, the one
approved first then read as approved at the other's head: land status
showed NEEDS-REVIEW and its hold reported a stale premise.

- ledger: newest_verdict_event_for_change reads a spec key for one change:
  that change's events and the spec's unbound ones; another change's event
  counts only when recorded at the head being judged.
- approval read (merge_gate_verdict_candidates, used by land status, ship
  and the train's member gate): once the change has a verdict of its own on
  the ledger, a spec key answers from the ledger through that reader and
  the spec's file is not read.
- hold premise (merge-hold list): reads the verdict as it concerns the
  hold's change.

A change with no ledger verdict of its own reads the spec record as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Merge branch 'integration' into story-2768-s2-run

* [AI:claude] fix(alloc): the ID counter is written with an explicit mode, whatever the umask (BUG-2555)

Under a umask of 002 (dell1's shells) every rewrite of
.git/aida-work-dispenser.toml left it 0664, and the next ID allocation
refused it as "unsafe WORK allocation state ... group- or other-writable".
The counter was written through write_atomic, whose staging file takes the
process umask.

- fs_atomic: write_atomic_mode stages the file, sets its mode on the open
  handle, then renames it over the target.
- The counter (FileDispenser create and save, raise_counter,
  restore_counter, bootstrap) and the node binding are written 0644.
- The refusal for a counter someone else made writable is unchanged: it is
  refused, not repaired.

* Merge commit '3350540dbab869a493924fe627364ed3a48ff9e4' into story-2745-seat-mail-sq

* [AI:claude] fix(gate): verdict selection reads only bound ledgers via write-ahead bindings (BUG-2531)

Writers persist bindings/<SPEC>/<CHANGE> under the append locks before
any append; a failed binding fails the append. An empty ledger is
certified by its first writer, whether or not the first events carry a
spec. The one-time bootstrap (aida doctor --heal --yes --category
gate-ledger-bindings) scans every change ledger under the exclusive
lock, writes bindings and publishes the completeness marker last.
Selection, ownership filtering and the effective view read only the
requested labels' bindings and the ledgers they name; a missing or
unsupported marker, a bound change without a ledger, or reviews without
a binding refuse and name the fix. Event format is 2: readers accept 1
and 2, and a writer refuses a ledger holding a newer format.

Ported onto integration: the shared discovery of a verdict listing
revalidates the marker, the bindings it listed and the stat identity of
each ledger it read; an unsafe unrelated ledger no longer blocks a
selection; doctor capacity wording and the store-writer inventory follow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

The gate-paths ratchet keeps approval-authority code on the protected

* [AI:claude] fix(train): read a PR with over 250 commits through the compare endpoint (Refs BUG-2583)

every train refused to open while one stayed open (#4038 had 254 commits
against main). Above 250 the scan now pages

declared count and its last commit to be the PR head, and re-reads the PR
to confirm the snapshot, as before. A mismatch stays unknown.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AI:claude] fix(gate): fence older ledger writers, bind every label, repair under a valid marker (BUG-2531)

Addresses the four blocking findings of the review at 87aac0b.

Older-writer exclusion is now enforced. Format 2 moves the ledger-wide
lock to .aida/gate-ledger.v2.lock. Before its first write, and before the
bootstrap certifies anything, a format 2 binary replaces the old lock
path .aida/gate-ledger.lock with a dangling link under the exclusive
format 2 lock and waits for every older writer that already holds the old
lock. An older binary opens or creates that path before every ledger
write, so each of its writes fails. The fence is part of the completeness
certificate: selection refuses a valid marker beside an old lock path
that is not the fence, and a writer that finds the fence down restores it
and withdraws the marker.

Binding completeness no longer withholds reviews. Every spec label an
event carries is bound: a label that is not a file-name key is bound
under ~<sha256 of the normalized label>. The ownership filter finds the
witnesses of every review copy, so it no longer drops a review (a refusal
included) whose label had no key.

The documented repair works under a valid marker. aida doctor reports,
and the heal rebuilds, older writers not fenced out, a binding whose
ledger is gone, a malformed bindings tree and, when the category is asked
for by name, a change ledger carrying a spec no binding names. The
rebuild withdraws the marker first, removes whatever is not a binding of
an existing change ledger, writes the bindings and publishes the marker
last.

Removes the stray runtime files aida-cli-lib/.aida/agents/handles/.lock
and aida-cli-lib/.aida/agents/other-2802564.toml.

* [AI:claude] fix(gate): full ledger read only on evidence of a lost binding (BUG-2531)

Advisor ruling 2026-11-14 13:06 on PR-4038: the full-read fallback fired
whenever a label had no by-spec hint, so the never-recorded alias of a
normal two-label selection read every change ledger again.

A selection now reads every change ledger only when the label's records
show a binding existed and is gone: its hint names a change the bindings
do not, or its bindings directory stands without a hint (the directory
outlives a deleted binding). A label with neither directory nor hint was
never recorded and reads no change ledger; a hint naming fewer changes
than the bindings is a lossy hint and reads only the bound ledgers.

The bootstrap leaves bound history as a writer does (each label's hint
names its bound changes) and removes a label directory it emptied, so
neither reads as a deletion afterwards.

Tests: two-label selection with an unrecorded alias reads exactly the
marker, one hint and one bound ledger (byte and parse counts, zero full
reads); a deleted binding with a stale or missing hint still finds the
newer refusal.

  whose lease names no spec keeps it too
- a spec is not reset in a pass that did not save and record its dead
  lane's work
- the patch a lease is released on is captured whole or not written
- a lease file that cannot be removed is reported as not released

* wip: BUG-2565 coalesce window (probe)

* [AI:claude] fix(pull): the coalescing lock is released before the pull runs (Refs BUG-2565)

The pull in flight held pull-<kind>.lock across the store-write window, so
the descriptor was open while hooks and git gc ran, and a pull started by a
hook of that pull waited out the whole coalescing budget for its own parent.

The lock is now taken only for the decision (wait, reuse or run) and closed
before the pull starts. The pull in flight is named by a marker file
(pid, process start identity, call token); a marker of a dead process is
ignored, a marker naming an ancestor of the caller means "run at once", and
the state is written before the marker is removed.

Tests: three lib tests (no lock held or open during the pull, an
ancestor's marker, a dead marker) and one aida-cli test driving a real
nested pull from a post-rewrite hook. The existing task_1717 tests are
unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AI:claude] fix(integration): origin calls route their credentials and --since is classified (Refs STORY-2772)

Two ratchets #4022 tripped at full tier:
- task_2001: the fetch and push of `origin integration` in sync-main/merge
  went through the raw git helper; they now use git_origin, which routes
  the remote's stored credentials through the environment.
- every_time_bound_flag_is_classified: `aida integration promotion-check
  --since` takes a git commit (the last promotion's cut), not a time; it is
  classified NotATimeBound with that reason.

* [AI:claude] fix(pull): the running-pull marker is judged through proc_identity (Refs BUG-2565)

The liveness ratchet (TASK-1750) forbids new private process-identity

and is judged by ProcIdentity::from_registry + observe.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AI:claude] fix(pull): a waiter never blocks past its budget on the decision lock (Refs BUG-2565)

Review of PR #4070 at 2b88689 (blocking P2): decision_lock used a blocking
lock_exclusive() and the ls-remote freshness probe ran under it, so a
waiter could block without bound and ignore AIDA_PULL_COALESCE_WAIT_SECS.

- decision_lock tries, then retries every POLL until the caller's deadline;
  a busy lock returns with the descriptor closed and the caller pulls.
- The freshness probe runs with no lock held, at most once; reuse is taken
  only after a revalidation under the lock (no pull in flight, no pull
  ended since), otherwise the caller decides again without reuse.
- The post-pull state write waits at most 5 s for the lock.

Tests: a stalled lock holder with WAIT_SECS=0 and =1 returns within the
budget; the probe runs with the decision lock free and the result is reused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AI:claude] fix(land): the salvage patch is one HEAD-to-worktree diff that applies back (Refs STORY-2768)

Review round 2 on PR #4058: the complete salvage appended git diff HEAD and
git diff --cached; HEAD already holds the staged changes, so a staged new
file or edit appeared twice and the patch did not apply. The salvage now
takes the HEAD diff alone. New round-trip test: a staged addition, a staged
edit, an edit staged then changed again and an untracked file, applied to a
clean checkout of HEAD, reproduce the worktree.

* [AI:claude] fix(pull): a marker of this very process is live without a procfs read (Refs BUG-2565)

One run in 42 of the bug_2565 lib set failed under load at bf9760f.

answer, which lets a waiter run beside the pull in flight; the marker's
own guard ends it with the call. The race test also allows 1.5 s, not
0.6 s, after every waiter has started.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AI:claude] test(pull): the lock probes allow a forked child's brief descriptor copy (Refs BUG-2565)

Under a 30-run stress at e5a7c03, the_pull_runs_with_no_coalesce_lock_held_or_open
failed twice: its try_lock found the lock taken. Another test thread's
child, between fork and exec, can hold a copy of a descriptor this module
already closed. The probes now retry for up to 2 s; a lock the module kept
across the pull would never come free while the pull waits. The
open-descriptor check is unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* [AI:claude] fix(pull): a marker with this PID is this process's only while its call runs (Refs BUG-2565)

Review of PR #4070 at bd02e36 (blocking P2): the e5a7c03 shortcut trusted
any marker whose PID equals std::process::id(), so after PID, boot or
namespace reuse a new pull waited out its budget on its own stale marker.
A process-local set of active call tokens now decides: the guard enters
the token before the marker is written and leaves it when the pull ends.
Markers of other processes keep the full procfs identity check.

Test: a marker with this PID and another boot, another start time, another
pid namespace, or this very identity from a call that is not running,
runs at once and its marker replaces the stale one.
